overview: Both reduce a solution's concentration, but serial dilution does it in successive steps to reach very high dilution factors accurately.
genZNote: Simple dilution: one big scoop of water. Serial dilution: a controlled staircase of smaller dilutions to get somewhere much more diluted, accurately.

aspects.label: Number of Steps
aspects.valueA: A single dilution step, from stock directly to the final concentration.
aspects.valueB: A stepwise series of dilutions, each using the previous dilution as the new stock.

aspects.label: Typical Purpose
aspects.valueA: Used when only a moderate dilution is needed.
aspects.valueB: Used to reach extremely high dilution factors accurately, common in microbial colony counting.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Diluting a stock solution 1:10 in one step.
aspects.valueB: Diluting 1:10, then 1:10 again, then again, to reach 1:1000 or higher for a viable count.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Serial dilution is the standard method used before spread plating or pour plating to get a countable number of bacterial colonies (30-300 CFU).
overlay.memoryTrick: Serial = a series of steps, each building on the last.
overlay.commonMisconception: Serial dilution isn't just 'more accurate' in general — it's specifically necessary because trying to measure one huge single dilution volume directly is impractical and error-prone.
